name: Wen T’ung
credit: “Bamboo in Monochrome Ink” by Wen Tong (11th century), National Palace Museum, Taipei · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Wen T’ung (1018–1079) was a Chinese poet, calligrapher and painter of the Northern Sung dynasty, best remembered for his ink paintings of bamboo, and a cousin and friend of the poet Su Tung-p’o.
The poems here are L. Cranmer-Byng’s versions in A Feast of Lanterns (1916), given under the poet’s name as spelled there.

poems.title: Morning
poems.author: Wen T’ung
poems.text:
Sunbeams through twinkling pinewoods cast
Their shadows on my window screen.
A night of clouds and rain is past
And, newly blue and freshly green,
The Dawn rebuilds my world at last.
Pear-tree and plum-tree shed their burden sweet,
And children's happy voices rouse the street.

poems.title: Evening
poems.author: Wen T’ung
poems.text:
Now pale flocks glimmer as they wind along;
Into the deep ravine the herd goes down;
The cold dumb pool awaits the nightly throng
Of wild geese wailing through the twilight brown.
With jars of new-made wine old farmer Wang
Gladdens the neighbours. Gloomy faces shine
And dark robes kindle to the flush of wine.
